_doc: Vesper Ashtongue, Occultist of the Black Choir: a fallen angel and the keeper of the Empty Throne arc. Pool 'vesper' (shop ids: occultist, oracle).

lines.text: Oh. A new note in the Pit's long song.
I am Vesper. I sang in the High Choir until I learned the hymn backwards. It burned my tongue to ash. The name stuck.
I sell rites, Sinbound. Small damnations. Each costs a few souls, and something else you will never notice is missing.

choices.text: Done. I have plenty to spare.

lines.label: what
lines.text: If I told you, you would notice. That would spoil it.

lines.label: deal
lines.text: Everyone says that. It is the most honest lie in the Pit.
Lilaeth. We stood three wings apart in the Choir. You had the higher voice.
And you had the better silence.
Sariel still sings your part, you know. Badly.
You died. I felt the note drop out of the song, and then come back in, off-key.
That is what the Font does. It returns you a little more out of tune each time. Heaven hates that more than anything.
Next time you go up, listen. Under the battle. The angels are singing.
Every hymn is a question, Sinbound. It is sung up, toward the Throne. And it should come back down changed. Answered.
They are not coming back down. I have listened for an age. Nothing comes back.

choices.text: Maybe the Throne is tired of them.
Why should I care what angels hear?

lines.label: tired
lines.text: Maybe. Or maybe there is no one there to be tired.

lines.label: care
lines.text: Because a soldier who stops hearing orders does one of two things. Deserts, or burns everything. Guess which one the Host is choosing.
You felled Sariel. I felt it in my teeth.
Did it say anything? At the end?

choices.text: It said the light was supposed to answer.
It begged someone to forgive it.

lines.label: answer
lines.text: ...Then it knows. Or it has begun to. Poor bright thing.

lines.label: forgive
lines.text: Someone. Anyone. Yes, that is how it starts. When you no longer know who to ask.

lines.label: nothing
lines.text: Liar. Heralds always have last words. It is their whole function.
The Lattice catches souls before they can fall to us. Have you wondered where it puts them?
Not into Heaven. I know Heaven's doors. None of them have opened in a very long time.
Ask the Clerk. Ledgers do not lie, even when their keepers do.
Hexbinder. You keep the names the angels forgot.
All of them.
Then tell me. Is there a name in your book that has been struck out? One name, at the very top of the first page?
...Yes. In a hand much older than mine.
I thought so. Do not read it aloud. Not here. Not yet.
Sit with me, Sinbound. This is not a rite. No charge.
I have listened to the silence long enough to be sure. The Throne is empty.
Not dead. Not sleeping. Empty. Perhaps since the Fall. Perhaps the Fall was simply the moment it emptied, and we were the first to notice.
The Archons noticed too. They have ruled from the steps ever since, relaying orders from a chair no one sits in.
And Hell remembers the Fall. Every demon is a witness that once there was Someone to fall from.
That is what the Last Dawn is for. Not to cleanse the world. To burn the witnesses. And the Lattice souls are the kindling.

lines.label: burn
lines.text: Spoken like a true demon. I will sing over the ashes.

lines.label: chair
lines.text: ...Yes. I suppose it is.
Be careful, {demon}. Everyone who has ever looked at that chair the way you are looking at it now has ended up falling.
I told Pip about the Throne. Which means the whole Pit knows by now.
Duchess Malphine has already sent someone up to measure it for a cushion.
Reaper. They say you harvest what Heaven sows.
Heaven sows a great deal and harvests nothing. Someone has to.
Then you will want to know where the Lattice takes its crop. Soon.
Every rite has a price. Yours is merely souls. For now.
Hush. Listen. Even the lava hums, if you are patient.
The Choir is loud tonight. Frightened, I think.
I can still hit the high notes. I simply choose not to.
You died off-key. Try again.
An empty chair is the loudest thing in all the worlds. Can you hear it?
Do you know what falling feels like, the first time? Not the Font. The real one. The Fall.
It feels like being let go of. That is all. A hand opens, and you understand it was never holding on very tightly.
When you reach the chair, {demon}, remember that. Nothing up there will hold you. Hold on yourself.
You came back without dying. The whole Choir felt it. Up there, I mean. They have changed key.
It is a minor key now. I could listen to it forever.
Sister. Hum with me. No one is listening, so it does not matter if we are flat.
You smell of old paper and older grudges. I approve.
The god in your chains sang to me last night. It is a terrible singer.
Ravager, please do not lean on the altar. It is load-bearing.
Reaper. Do you ever reap songs? I have some I would like gone.
Your swarm hums in a key I have not heard since the Fall. I find it oddly soothing.
Nhazgul. Were you anything, before the flies?
A man who let things rot. Food. Friends. A city. I sat in the middle of it and called it mine.
And now the rot sits in you and calls you its own. Heaven would call that justice.
Heaven calls a lot of things justice. The flies call it home.
Iscariel. You opened the Gate the night I fell through it. I never thanked you. I am still deciding whether to.
Iscariel. You opened the First Gate. I fell through it a moment later. Did you see me go?
I saw everyone go. I held the doors and counted, the way Kesh does now. You were the first of the Choir through. Lilaeth was close behind.
...So someone saw. I went first so she would know there was somewhere to land. I thought no one knew.
Nobody falls unseen, Vesper. That was the point of opening the door.
